    Quality & Manufacturing

    Quality and manufacturing

    Every product runs through the same sequence in-house, from raw-material procurement to standardized, packed and documented batch.

    Process

    Manufacturing sequence

    Run in-house from specification to finished product. The extraction route — solvent, supercritical CO₂ or steam distillation — depends on the product and the fraction required.

    1. 01

      Procurement

      Raw material sourced and checked against specification before processing.

    2. 02

      Extraction

      Solvent, CO₂ or steam-distillation route chosen for the product and target fraction.

    3. 03

      Filtration

      Removal of plant solids from the extract.

    4. 04

      Concentration

      Solvent recovery and concentration of the extract.

    5. 05

      Drying

      Conversion to the required physical form where applicable.

    6. 06

      Standardization

      Adjusted to the specified marker-compound content.

    7. 07

      Packaging

      Packed and labelled per order, with batch documentation.

    Quality control

    Checks on every batch

    The two things every inquiry eventually comes down to: what was tested, and what documentation comes with it.

    Batch traceability
    Every batch is traceable from raw material through to the finished product.
    Raw material testing
    Incoming botanical material is tested before it enters production.
    Finished goods testing
    Batch-level checks before anything is cleared to ship.
    Documentation
    Certificate of Analysis per batch; specification sheet, TDS and SDS on request.

    Documentation

    Documents supplied

    Request any of these from a product page or through the inquiry form.

    DocumentCoversProvided
    Certificate of Analysis (COA)Test results for the batch suppliedWith every batch
    Specification sheetThe agreed specification for the product and gradeOn request
    Technical Data Sheet (TDS)Technical properties, handling and use of the productOn request
    Safety Data Sheet (SDS)Safety, storage and transport informationOn request

    Process capability

    Flow and vapour-phase chemistry

    Used for our cosmetic ingredients range of ketones and acetophenones.

    Vapour phase chemistry is especially suited for hazardous, exothermic, and high-temperature processes, offering better reaction control, faster kinetics, and minimized solvent usage — aligning with both economic and environmental goals.

    High-pressure operations
    Up to 50 bar
    High-temperature reactions
    Up to 600 °C
    Flexible reactor configurations
    For rapid scale-up from pilot to commercial scale

    Reaction types

    • Alcohol → aldehyde / ketone
    • Ammoxidation
    • Dehydrogenation
    • Hydrogenation
    • Decarboxylation / decarbonylation

    Quality questions we are asked most

    Can I get a Certificate of Analysis?

    Yes — COAs are provided per batch alongside your order.

    Can you formulate to a custom purity or specification?

    Yes. Share your specification or target application and we will scope a custom formulation or grade.

    Do you provide samples?

    Get in touch with the product you are interested in and we can discuss sample availability.

    Do you ship internationally?

    Yes. Let us know your destination when you reach out, and we will confirm shipping options and documentation.

    Ask about our process

    Tell us the product you are evaluating and the documentation your quality team needs. We will confirm what is available for your grade and market.
